data.title: Chile's Codelco reports 9M pre-tax loss of $1.4 bln
data.description:
Chile's Codelco, one of the world's largest copper producers, on Friday reported a pre- tax loss of $1.4 billion for the first nine months of 2026, compared to $607 million profit posted in the same period a year earlier.

The state-owned miner's own copper production totaled 853,000 metric tons in the January-September period, down from the 937,000 tons reported a year earlier.

data.title: Target Launches Cyber Monday Sale With Discounts Of Up To 50%
data.description:
MINNEAPOLIS (dpa-AFX) - Retailer Target Corp. (TGT) announced on Friday that its online-only Cyber Monday sale will begin on November 30, offering discounts of up to 50% on thousands of products across categories including toys, electronics, apparel, beauty and home goods.

The company said the promotion will be available through Target.com and the Target app starting at 2 a.m. Central Time.

Target said the event will also feature its AI-powered shopping assistant, Ask Target, and an expanded assortment from its Target Plus third-party marketplace.

The retailer said Target Circle members will be eligible for its annual promotion offering 10% off Target gift cards on December 5 and December 6.

On NYSE, shares of Target were down 0.03% at $172.16.

data.title: W.Africa Crude-Market ends week on a quiet note on freight rates
data.description:
The West African crude oil market ended the week on a quiet note, as freight rates continued to weigh on activity.

  • Freight rates are expected to keep climbing which is dampening differentials and market activity, a trade source said.

  • Nigeria is expected to export slightly more of its four main crude grades from December, preliminary programmes seen by Reuters showed.

  • A handful of Angolan cargoes for December are still available, the source said.

data.title: Dutch drugmaker Lundbeck reportedly eyeing deals in psychedelic space
data.description:
Companies focused on psychedelic medicines traded higher on Friday after The Wall Street Journal reported that Dutch drugmaker Lundbeck is exploring deals in that space.

Notable gainers include Helus Pharma , Compass Pathways , Definium Therapeutics , GH Research , and Bright Minds Biosciences .

“We are mapping the space, and we have quite active conversations around what is happening in this landscape,” Lundbeck CEO Charl van Zyl said during an interview. “There are some more late-stage companies, and then there are also obviously more early-stage-profiled companies. We keep looking at all these options,” he added.

His remarks came amid growing interest in psychedelic space among big pharma following a series of favorable regulatory measures under the Trump administration.

Earlier this year, President Donald Trump issued an executive order to speed up research into psychedelic-based drugs, a move aimed at making substances such as psilocybin, LSD, and MDMA widely available in the U.S.

In September, Eli Lilly acquired psychedelic drugmaker AtaiBeckley for more than $2.8B. “We also like that space,” van Zyl said. “We think it’s got a lot of clinical relevance, and the body of evidence has increased a lot, so we continue to look in that space.”

Known for antidepressants such as citalopram and escitalopram, Lundbeck has shifted its focus away from psychiatric therapies to rare neurological diseases and migraine in recent years. One of its most advanced candidates includes a rare epilepsy treatment called bexicaserin, which it added in 2024 from its $2.6B acquisition of U.S.-based Longboard Pharma.

Lundbeck's strategy is not solely reliant on M&A, according to van Zyl, who added that the company is also seeking deals to strengthen its product pipeline.

“As they say, we continue to shop even if we’re not hungry,” Van Zyl said. “We continue to look for things that will allow us to bolster where we have know-how and where we have expertise.”

data.title: Gold’s Biggest Challenge Is No Longer The Fed, Says Economist Robin Brooks – ‘We Are Back To Oil As The Principal Risk Factor For Gold’
data.description:
Key points:
  • Growing concerns over the AI sector could weaken the U.S. economy, reducing the case for further interest rate hikes, Brooks said.
  • The economist estimates that a 10% jump in Brent crude prices could trigger a 4% decline in gold.
  • Traders are pricing in a 99.2% probability of another quarter-point hike in December, compared to 88.6% a week ago.

Economist Robin Brooks believes the Federal Reserve’s hawkish stance has already been played out as a catalyst for gold, with bullion’s near-term outlook now depending on the “hot” war.

In a Substack post on Friday, Brooks said he was “shocked by this month’s fall in gold prices,” noting that rising real interest rates accounted for only a small portion of the losses. “Real rates have plateaued, which is just another way of saying that Fed hawkishness is close to maxed out.”

Spot gold fell nearly 8% this month through Thursday. At the time of writing, it was up 1.75% to $3,628.94 per ounce. Gold futures expiring in January 2027 jumped 2.7% to $3,646.20 per ounce.

The SPDR Gold Shares ETF (GLD) was up 1.3%.

“I don’t think a return to a “hot” war is near and – in the big picture – the conflict is winding down. But it’s also true Iran keeps taking potshots at Western ships in the Strait of Hormuz, so this is very much a live risk. We’re back to oil as the principal risk factor for gold,” he noted.

Brooks Says Further Rate Hikes Unlikely

Brooks said growing concerns over the AI sector could weaken the U.S. economy, reducing the likelihood that September and October’s surge in oil prices will lead to broader inflation and further rate hikes.

The Fed raised interest rates by 25 basis points in September, its first hike since 2023, before holding rates steady at 3.75%-4% in October.

However, traders are pricing in a 99.2% probability of another quarter-point hike in December, compared to 88.6% a week ago.

Oil Prices Hold The Key

Brooks estimates that a 10% increase in Brent crude prices could trigger a 4% decline in gold, with silver potentially falling 8%. “We’re back to oil as the principal risk factor for gold,” Brooks said.

On Thursday, U.S. President Donald Trump reportedly said that victory against Iran would be achieved “whenever I want it,” and that he is giving the country “a chance to be smart,” but expressed doubts over a deal.

Brent crude futures for January 2027 deliveries traded 2% lower at $94.59 per barrel, but have gained about 28% since the U.S.-Israeli strikes hit Iran on February 28.

data.title: EU wheat extends gains on Black Sea disruption
data.description:
Euronext wheat prices climbed to fresh one-month highs on Friday as ongoing war disruption to Black Sea trade maintained expectations of strong demand for European Union supplies.

However, Euronext futures pared gains after news of a Black Sea truce proposed by Ukraine to allow food exports.

March wheat , the most active position on Euronext, was up 0.6% at €239.25 ($262.70) a metric ton at 1642 GMT.

The contract earlier reached €242.75 for its highest since October 20, surpassing previous one-month peaks this week.

Front-month December wheat rose 0.4% to €244.75 a ton after touching another one-month high at €248.50.

A Russian attack on two cargo ships carrying grain near the Ukrainian Black Sea port of Odesa this week has kept the focus on disruption to grain trade, reinforcing expectations of more demand shifting towards European Union exporting countries.

"It's a combination of war news and a heavy EU export programme," a futures broker said of the Euronext rally. "The winter weather is also set to slow the shipment of Russian grain."

Expana analysts raised their forecast for EU soft wheat exports this season and reduced their outlook for EU soft wheat stocks to a six-year low.

But comments by Ukraine's foreign minister on Friday, saying Kyiv has proposed a Black Sea ceasefire to enable food exports, restrained prices by reviving the possibility of some kind of safe shipping arrangement in the zone.

A recent round of negotiations between Russia and Ukraine had contributed to prices falling to multi-month lows.

Chicago wheat rallied on Friday as the US market reopened following Thursday's Thanksgiving holiday, with the market buoyed by higher-than-expected weekly US export sales.

Gains on broader financial markets as AI-related investor worries subsided also helped to underpin grain markets.

A large wheat import tender being held by Pakistan, which is seeking to buy 800,000 tons with a bidding deadline on Monday, was awaited for a fresh gauge of export competition.

Nearly all recently sown soft wheat in France remained in good condition as of Monday, data from farm office FranceAgriMer showed.

Frosts in northern France on Friday were not expected to pose any risks to crops, traders said.

($1 = 0.9107 euros)

data.title: Gulf Airlines Face Fuel-Cost, Competition Risks — Market Talk
data.description: Gulf airlines' earnings recovery hinges on lower fuel prices and easing geopolitical tensions, Bahrain-based investment bank SICO says, noting jet-fuel prices rose 73% between 4Q 2025 and 3Q 2026. data.title: Tech Stocks Rise as Investors Take a Break From AI Jitters — WSJ
Stocks hit the sales early: S&P 500 up 1.5% on Black Friday
data.description:
The S&P 500 (SP500) was on track for one of its strongest Black Friday performances on record, rising 1.1% in morning trading, according to data shared by Ryan Detrick of Carson Investment Research.

“Two hours to go, but this is currently one of the better Black Friday returns ever for the S&P 500,” Detrick wrote on X.

Data posted by Detrick showed the S&P 500's strongest Black Friday gains included a 1.8% rise in 1971, a 1.7% advance in 2007, and gains of 1.5% in both 1984 and 2000. The index also rose 1.4% in 1963 and 1.3% in 2012.

The 2026 advance was among 12 Black Friday sessions since 1950 in which the index gained more than 1%. Its 1.1% rise was in line with gains recorded in 1956, 1957, and 1958. The 2026 figure is based on the index's intraday price and does not represent its final closing return.

At the time of writing, the blue-chip Dow was last +1.2%, the benchmark S&P 500 (SP500) was last +1.5%, and the tech-focused Nasdaq Composite was last +2%.

data.title: Global measles deaths fall to historic low in 2025, WHO says
data.description:
By Siddhi Mahatole and Christy Santhosh

Global measles deaths hit a historic low in 2025, the World Health Organization said on Friday, although millions of children still missed vaccinations and outbreaks persisted in dozens of countries.

The UN health agency estimated 9.8 million measles cases and about 72,000 deaths worldwide in 2025 — down 74% from 37.8 million cases in 2000, with deaths falling roughly 91% from about 769,000.

WHO said global measles immunization rates remained largely unchanged in 2025, but cautioned the trend hides declines in some regions, including the Americas, where coverage has dropped from levels above 90% before the COVID-19 pandemic.

Several countries have recently lost their measles elimination status, showing that without high vaccination coverage, surveillance and political will, the virus can "quickly regain a foothold," WHO said.

Twenty-nine million children were unvaccinated or under-vaccinated against measles in 2025, the agency said on a press call. WHO estimated that 20.8 million infants missed a first dose of vaccine and another 8.3 million missed a second dose.

"The recent setbacks we've seen are not a failure of the measles vaccine, they're a failure to reach every child with the vaccine," said Dr. Kate O'Brien, director of WHO's Department of Immunization, Vaccines and Biologicals.

WHO said 59 countries reported large or disruptive outbreaks in 2025, compared with 61 in 2024 and 58 in 2023.

CALL FOR INVESTMENT

O'Brien called for countries to "double down on the investments in their programs," to ensure that the vaccine is available at times and places that people can easily access.

WHO warned that immunization and surveillance programmes face increasing financial pressures even as the costs of closing immunity gaps and responding to outbreaks rise.

O'Brien said the measles vaccine delivers one of the highest returns on investment of any vaccine, calling it "a best buy."

data.title: US stock market today: Dow Jones jumps 510 points, S&P 500 rises 1.2%, Nasdaq gains 1.7%
data.description:
US stocks rose on Friday (November 27), with investors looking to end a turbulent, holiday-shortened trading week on a positive note.

The Dow Jones Industrial Average gained 510 points, or 1%, while the S&P 500 advanced 1.2% and the Nasdaq Composite climbed 1.7% amid a volatile trading week, capping an equally turbulent month for Wall Street.

Technology stocks led the recovery, with shares of “Magnificent Seven” members Meta Platforms and Amazon rising around 3% each. Chipmaker Broadcom gained 2%, while artificial intelligence company Anthropic advanced more than 8%.

Wall Street's three major indices were also on track for strong weekly gains. Ahead of Friday's session, the Dow was up 5% for the week, putting it on course for its biggest weekly gain since April 2025. The S&P 500 had advanced nearly 5%, while the Nasdaq Composite had climbed more than 5%.

The week kicked off with Jensen Huang getting reinstated as CEO at Nvidia, a move that sent the stock up 31% during Monday’s session and drove the S&P 500 and Nasdaq Composite to post their best days since April 2025. The Dow Jones Industrial Average advanced more than 1,400 points, or roughly 3%.

Since then, however, the S&P 500 and Nasdaq have come under pressure as Nvidia and other AI-related stocks have given back some of Monday’s gains.

Some Wall Street analysts believe the recent market weakness has been driven less by long-term concerns over artificial intelligence (AI) valuations and more by expectations of further interest rate hikes by the Federal Reserve.

The latest Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index data released this week reinforced market expectations of multiple rate hikes in the coming months.

US markets were closed on Thursday for the Thanksgiving holiday and are scheduled to close early at 1 p.m. ET on Friday.

Meanwhile, copper extended its recovery, while oil prices were on track for their first weekly gain this month as escalating attacks on energy infrastructure and tankers in the Middle East fuelled concerns over potential supply disruptions.

In China, stocks surged to their best session in more than two years after authorities issued a rare midday statement pledging support for the markets.

data.title: RBI sets time-bound process for banks to freeze suspicious accounts, mandates 7-day response window for customers
data.description:
The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) on November 27 issued final directions mandating a time-bound procedure for banks to identify highly suspicious transactions and accounts, including those linked to money mule activity and cyber-enabled financial frauds. Under the new framework, banks will have to give customers seven calendar days to explain suspicious transactions, while the bank will get another seven days to examine the response and decide whether to remove or continue the debit hold.

The directions require banks to remove a debit hold on the 31st day from referring a case to the jurisdictional police authority if no valid instruction requiring its continuation is received within 30 calendar days. However, this is subject to the bank being satisfied with its enhanced due diligence (EDD).

The directions have been issued separately for commercial banks and small finance banks (SFBs). They will come into effect from July 1, 2027, or an earlier date as decided by an individual bank.

Banks to follow uniform procedure for debit holds

Under the final directions, banks will have to put in place technological or other solutions to identify highly suspicious transactions and accounts based on objective parameters, while ensuring that genuine customers are not wrongly identified.

Banks may place a debit hold on the amount involved in a suspicious transaction or on the entire account, depending on the circumstances. However, an account-level hold must be based on a high degree of suspicion that the transaction or account is related to an offence specified under the Prevention of Money Laundering Act, 2002, a financial fraud or terrorist financing. Such holds will also require approval at an appropriately higher level.

The RBI has specifically said that "mechanical application of hold at account level shall be avoided".

Once a debit hold is placed, banks must promptly notify customers through digital channels. Where communication is through physical mode, the notification must be sent by the end of the next working day.

The notification must specify the reasons for the hold, the process for its removal, the contact details of the concerned officer and seek an explanation, along with supporting documents, if any, within seven calendar days from the date of the debit hold.

Banks must examine the explanation and documentation and take a decision within seven calendar days of receiving the customer's response. If satisfied with the explanation, the bank must remove the hold. Otherwise, it must continue the hold and report the matter, along with reasons, to the jurisdictional police authority.

If the customer does not submit an explanation within seven calendar days of being notified, the bank must continue the hold and refer the matter to the police authority with reasons. Banks will also have to undertake enhanced due diligence of the account after making the reference.

RBI drops Rs 1,000 threshold after stakeholder feedback

The final directions follow RBI's September 11 draft amendment to the Know Your Customer (KYC) Directions. In its statement on stakeholder feedback, the central bank accepted the suggestion to remove the proposed minimum threshold of Rs 1,000 for identifying suspected money mule transactions.

Stakeholders had pointed out that small-value transactions could also form part of organised money laundering and that a fixed threshold could encourage fraudsters to split transactions into smaller amounts to avoid detection.

RBI also broadened the scope of the definition by removing references to deposit accounts and the recruitment of third parties acting as money mules. The final directions define a money mule account as one used on behalf of another person, knowingly or unknowingly, to receive, layer or transfer proceeds of an offence specified in the Schedule to the Act, financial fraud or transactions involving terrorist financing.

Banks cannot continue holds indefinitely without valid instructions

RBI did not accept stakeholders' suggestions to extend the period available to law enforcement agencies to respond to 90 days or allow banks to continue debit holds indefinitely based on their internal risk assessment.

Explaining its decision, the central bank said, "Continuing the hold in the absence of an instruction from the LEA / Competent Authority would be akin to placing a permanent restriction on the account, the cost of which is borne by the customer."

Under the final directions, if no instruction specifically requiring continuation of the debit hold is received within 30 calendar days of the reference to the jurisdictional police authority, the bank must remove the hold on the 31st day, provided it is satisfied with its enhanced due diligence. If it is not satisfied, the hold may continue and the existing instructions on inoperative accounts under the respective Responsible Business Conduct Directions will apply.

Any instruction issued under the relevant statutory provisions by the jurisdictional police authority or another competent authority, including a court or tribunal empowered to issue directions relating to bank accounts, must be complied with by the bank.

The directions also require banks to designate nodal officers to handle complaints arising from the SOP. Their contact details must be displayed on bank websites and at branches. Complaints must be acknowledged upon receipt and resolved within 30 calendar days.

Banks will also have to maintain records relating to accounts and amounts placed under debit hold, including the reasons for the hold, dates of placement and release, and correspondence with customers and police authorities, for five years from the date of placing the hold.
